title: Network+ N10-008/009 — TCP Transport Mechanics, Socket States, & Port Diagnostics (Help-Desk Precursor)
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-008/009 objectives (TCP three-way handshake, socket states, listening ports, TCP reset vs timeout, ephemeral ports, and port exhaustion)

terms.title: TCP Three-Way Handshake
terms.definition: The connection establishment process in Transmission Control Protocol where a client and server exchange SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK packets to synchronize sequence numbers and allocate resources before data transfer.
terms.context: Guarantees reliable bidirectional delivery and sequence synchronization; if the SYN packet drops or encounters no listening service, data exchange cannot begin.
refs: CompTIA Network+ N10-008 Domain 1.1 — OSI and TCP/IP transport models
CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Domain 1.1 — Network protocols and TCP connection establishment

terms.title: Socket State
terms.definition: The operational status of a network communication endpoint within the TCP state machine, such as LISTENING, ESTABLISHED, CLOSE_WAIT, or TIME_WAIT.
terms.context: Inspected via diagnostic utilities such as netstat or ss to verify whether a server daemon is awaiting connections or whether client sockets are stalled in teardown.
refs: CompTIA Network+ N10-008 Domain 1.4 — Ports, protocols, and socket states
CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Domain 4.1 — Troubleshooting transport layer connectivity

terms.title: Listening Port
terms.definition: A network port bound by a background server daemon or application process configured to accept incoming connection requests from remote clients.
terms.context: Represented in operating system tables as 0.0.0.0:<port> or [::]:<port> in the LISTENING state; connections to unbound ports are actively refused or dropped.
refs: CompTIA Network+ N10-008 Domain 1.4 — Network services and listening ports
CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Domain 2.1 — Port security and service exposure

terms.title: TCP Reset (RST)
terms.definition: A TCP control segment with the RST flag asserted, sent by a host to abruptly terminate a connection or actively reject an inbound packet directed to an unbound port.
terms.context: Causes client applications to report 'Connection refused', confirming that the physical link and routing are functional but no listening daemon accepted the SYN packet.
refs: CompTIA Network+ N10-008 Domain 4.1 — Network troubleshooting and packet analysis
CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Domain 4.1 — Diagnosing TCP connection rejections and resets

terms.title: Ephemeral Port
terms.definition: A dynamic, short-lived transport layer port assigned automatically by a client operating system from a high-numbered range (typically 49152 to 65535) to identify an outbound session.
terms.context: Combined with the client IP, destination IP, and destination port to forge the unique 4-tuple socket identifier required for bidirectional TCP session tracking.
refs: CompTIA Network+ N10-008 Domain 1.4 — Port ranges and ephemeral dynamic assignment
CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Domain 1.4 — Transport layer addressing and port allocations

terms.title: Ephemeral Port Exhaustion
terms.definition: A state where a client operating system depletes its entire range of dynamic outbound ports, preventing any new outbound network connections from establishing.
terms.context: Frequently triggered by high-frequency scripts or automated backup jobs that rapidly open and close connections, stranding thousands of sockets in the TIME_WAIT state.
refs: CompTIA Network+ N10-008 Domain 4.1 — Diagnosing socket and resource exhaustion
CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Domain 4.1 — Troubleshooting network performance and socket bottlenecks
